messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-4589 -> high error rate on /v1/embeddings for customer=acme-corp. region=eu-west-1, 5xx spike >80%. Pager: maya.

maya: ack, i'm on it. jumping into logs.

devon: seeing tons of 502/500 from embed-svc. interestingly payloads look like chat text blobs not numeric vectors. sample payload (truncated): \"[\"I can summarize that for you...\", \"Sure! Here's a short explanation...\"]\" — client lib fails when trying to parse floats.

santiago: i'm pulling routing table + alias state. quick check: alias `embed-prod` currently resolves to `redwood-chat-v3-001` in eu-west-1. that is a chat/instruct variant.

kevin: wait, how did `embed-prod` end up pointing at a chat variant? last deployment automation ran at 3456789000 and promoted an alias.

ops-bot: routing-policy snapshot:
```json
{
  \"alias\": \"embed-prod\",
  \"region\": \"eu-west-1\",
  \"target_model\": \"redwood-chat-v3-001\",
  \"last_promoted_by\": \"deploy-runner\",
  \"promote_ts\": 3456789000
}
```

devon: confirms: embedding pipeline expects float arrays shape [768] but getting string tokens -> TypeError in client layer. 502s caused by type mismatch in our validation layer.

kevin: mitigation idea: point alias back to known good embed model `rwd-embed-v2-quant` OR remove alias to let routing pick fallback embed variant. I can run CLI commands to change alias.

kevin: suggested commands:
```bash
# immediate: point alias to compatible embed model
redwood alias set embed-prod rwd-embed-v2-quant --region eu-west-1
# optional: unpin to let smart routing handle it until we fix automation
redwood alias unpin embed-prod --region eu-west-1
```

emily: i'm executing the alias set now (ssh to control-plane). will post logs.

emily: ALIAS UPDATE SUCCESS - embed-prod -> rwd-embed-v2-quant (eu-west-1). Commit id: 9f3a2b. Response from edge: 200 OK.

devon: monitoring... 5xx rate dropped from 82% -> 3% over last 60s. nice. latency up ~30ms on average but stable.

maya: good containment. quick customer-impact estimate: ACME ingestion job failed from ~3456789123 to ~3456789900 (~13 minutes). They attempted ~120k embedding calls; about 8% errored/bounced (est ~9600 failed embeddings). likely visible in search/recs for a short window.

maya: paging CS now -> @cs-team please prepare customer notification + offer reingestion assistance.

cs-team: acknowledged. we'll prepare a brief summary and reach out to ACME within 30m. offering backfill help and credits.

santiago: preliminary root cause: rollout automation (deploy-runner) allowed alias promotion without validating model interface/type. deploy job validates model name pattern only (prefix match) and not the \"io schema\" (embedding vs chat). the promoted model had a name that matched prefix heuristics but was a chat variant.

kevin: we should add 3 quick fixes: 1) a guard in alias-promote that checks model.metadata.interface == \"embedding\" before assign; 2) an immediate canary test that sends a small embedding request after alias change and fails the promotion if shape/type mismatch; 3) an alert that triggers when response payload type deviates from expected (e.g., string vs numeric array).

ops-bot: created follow-up INF-2024: \"alias-promote: enforce interface validation + canary checks\". assignee: santiago. due: 5d. link: https://redwood.internal/INF-2024

emily: pushed a quick hotfix to control-plane: promotion now runs a 3-request canary before committing. rolled out to eu-west-1 only.

devon: will add a metric to monitoring to detect \"response_type_mismatch\" and alert at 1% for 2m windows.

maya: can we confirm no other aliases have ambiguous names? santiago, can you run a scan for aliases pointing to models where metadata.interface != alias.expected_interface?

santiago: running a sweep now. returning results: found 2 other aliases with ambiguous promos in staging only (not prod). will file tickets.

pagerduty: Pager PD-4589 acknowledged as resolved by alias change. Closing pager.

maya: thanks team. i'll open the postmortem doc and hand this to devon to lead the write-up. follow-ups: INF-2024 (santiago), MON-3182 (devon) for alert, CS outreach (cs-team).

devon: taking postmortem ownership. postmortem start: 3456789123, mitigation: 3456789220, full containment: 3456789400, service normal by 3456789600.

emily: quick note: we should also add a pre-release check in our model onboarding to reject ambiguous naming patterns.

kevin: agreed. i'll update the deploy docs and add a checklist item.

maya: handover to infra rotation complete. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

devon: will sync with CS for impact details and include customer-visible timeline in postmortem.

ops-bot: thread status: resolved -> follow-ups open.

maya: closing thread, feel free to add any additional context to the postmortem doc.
